pick.name: Phone Link (Link to Windows) + Google Quick Share
pick.what: Phone Link: texts, calls, notifications, recent photos, apps on PC; Quick Share: fast E2E-encrypted file transfer both ways
pick.why: Both are first-party and free; Phone Link is built into Windows 11 and Quick Share needs no app on Android 6+
pick.free_limits: Free; Phone Link needs Android 10+, same Wi-Fi, a personal Microsoft account (no work/school accounts)

alts.name: KDE Connect
alts.what: Open-source phone<->PC notifications, clipboard, files, remote input; no account
alts.why: Wins if company policy blocks signing a personal Microsoft account into Windows: works over local network with no cloud identity
alts.windows_fit: native (Microsoft Store or offline installer) + Android (Play/F-Droid)

alts.name: Google Quick Share for Windows (alone)
alts.why: Minimal footprint if you only need files

candidates.name: KDE Connect
candidates.verdict: No account needed; best under strict IT policy

candidates.name: Samsung Quick Share
candidates.verdict: Only for Samsung PCs; Google's version does not support them

decision: Phone Link plus Quick Share is the most capable free pairing. Phone Link needs a personal Microsoft account on Windows, which company policy may not allow on a managed laptop; in that case use KDE Connect (no account, local network) plus Quick Share.
details: Do not mirror personal phone notifications onto a device IT can inspect if that bothers you.

verify.note: Phone Link: Android 10+, Microsoft account, work/school accounts not supported - confirmed on MS page. Same-Wi-Fi not stated on that page.
